title: Come, Lord Jesus
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Come, Lord Jesus is the church’s prayerful longing for the return of Christ. It expresses worship, hope, faithfulness, and holy desire for the Lord to complete His saving purpose.
summary: Come, Lord Jesus is the church’s prayerful longing for the return of Christ. It expresses worship, hope, faithfulness, and holy desire for the Lord to complete His saving purpose.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the One for whom the church waits. The final prayer of Scripture is directed toward His coming, because He alone will judge evil, restore all things, and dwell with His people forever.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Bible ends with longing: “Come, Lord Jesus.” This prayer gathers together the church’s hope, worship, endurance, and desire for the Lord Himself.

To pray for Christ’s coming is to long for more than escape from trouble. It is to long for Jesus, His kingdom, His justice, His presence, His restoration, and His glory.

This longing is Spirit-formed and bride-like. The Spirit and the bride say, “Come.” The church waits not as a detached observer, but as a beloved people awaiting the Bridegroom.

The prayer also shapes present faithfulness. Those who long for Christ’s return are called to holiness, mission, patience, and endurance until He comes.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Believers can become attached to this age, numbed by delay, or consumed by fear of the future. The prayer “Come, Lord Jesus” re-centers the heart on Christ Himself.

This doctrine gives language to Christian longing. The church does not merely wait for better circumstances; she waits for her Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pray with the church, “Come, Lord Jesus.” Let that longing purify your desires, strengthen your endurance, and deepen your worship. Live faithfully while you wait, inviting others to come to the Savior before He comes in judgment and glory.
